extract: Zuldazar (/zuːl.ˈdə.ˌzɑɹ/ zool-DƏ-ZAHR), or Zuldazar City, the city of gold is the seat of the Zandalari Empire and the most ancient city on Azeroth. This massive, golden temple city is considered the jewel of all troll civilizations. Built atop the highest peaks of Zandalar in a series of giant ziggurats, its majestic pyramids tower above the jungle canopy and its indomitable navy controls the South Seas. It is here that, every six years, envoys from all the troll tribes convey in order to share information and discuss matters that may affect the entire troll race. Recently, the kingdom has faced attacks by forces both within and without, with the city's gates assailed by the rising tide of a relentless enemy, the blood trolls.

Built atop the highest peaks of [[Zandalar]] in a series of giant ziggurats,{{Ref WoWCV1|70}} its majestic pyramids tower above the jungle canopy and its [[Golden Fleet|indomitable navy]] controls the [[South Seas]]. It is here that, every six years, envoys from all the [[troll]] tribes convey in order to share information and discuss matters that may affect the entire troll race.[[Troll Compendium/Other Trolls#Zandalar Tribe|The Troll Compendium: Zandalar Tribe]] Recently, the kingdom has faced attacks by forces both within and without, with the [[Blood Gate|city's gates]] assailed by the rising tide of a relentless enemy, the [[blood troll]]s.[[:File:Blizzard Museum - Zandalar.jpg]] ==Description== [[File:Zuldazar 1.jpg|Zuldazar|thumb]] Nestled deep in [[Zandalar]]'s primal jungle, Zuldazar is a remnant of the once-mighty [[Zandalari Empire|Zandalar empire]]. A vast coastline surrounds Zuldazar to the south, east, and west, offering bountiful opportunities for fishing, boating, swimming, and treasure hunting. To the north are the marshland of [[Nazmir]], and the deserts of [[Vol'dun]]. High above the jungle canopies, the [[Golden Throne]] serves as Zuldazar's city center, with some of the most breathtaking views in the region. It is from here that [[Rastakhan]], king of the Zandalari, rules. A vast, ancient cityscape of interconnected terraces sprawls out below, dotted with temples devoted to the [[loa]], which are maintained by their loyal servants. Visitors can find anything they need for an extended stay in the heart of [[Dazar'alor]] at the center of the city. Facilities include an inn, portals to all major Horde cities along with Dalaran, profession trainers, a bank, training dummies, vendors, and more. It’s easy to get lost this ancient, multileveled city—but that only emphasizes its vastness and grandeur. There are thousands of steps throughout Zuldazar. One needs to keep an eye out or risk plummeting into one of the many thunderous waterfalls surrounding the city. Worshipped as deities by the Zandalar trolls, many of the temples dedicated to them can be often found on high ground or mountain peaks, which are viewed as sacred ground by the devout. In the southern part of city at its lowest point is the expansive [[Port of Zandalar]]. It is here that the Zandalari berth their [[Golden Fleet|mighty fleet]] and traders from around [[Azeroth]] sell their wares and services. Zandalar's rich tapestry of flora and fauna deserve research and cataloguing. The Zandalari have shown themselves to be able beast masters, having domesticated many of the creatures that roam the land. Some of these serve as helpful allies to the Zandalari; others prove obstacles to those who would seek to exploit the jungle's resources. Tamed Ravasaurs, Brutosaurs, Pterrodax, and Direhorns make up just a portion of their menagerie. There are countless other wild beasts that make their homes in surrounding jungles, from Muddy Riverbeasts to Roaming Nibblers. Following the [[Golden Road]] from the city and up into the mountains to the west will eventually lead to [[Atal'Dazar]]. These ancient pyramids have served as the resting place for Zandalari kings for millennia. With each passing ruler, new rooms are constructed to house the deceased’s vast wealth. Zuldazar has mountains reaching altitudes so high that it is hard for most species to breathe.[[Ji'arak#Adventure Guide]] ==History== ===Ancient times=== On [[Kalimdor (landmass)|primordial Kalimdor]], a series of peaks and plateaus located in the southern part of the continent was home to many [[Wild God]]s. Due to their reverence for these beings, which they called [[loa|"loa"]], the early [[troll]]s settled on the holy mountain range and gave it the name "Zandalar", building small encampments upon its slopes. The most powerful group of trolls was called the [[Zandalar tribe]]. Its members claimed nearly all of Zandalar's tallest plateaus, believing them to be sacred ground. Atop the highest peaks they built a small cluster of crude shrines, which over time grew into a bustling temple city known as Zuldazar.''[[World of Warcraft: Chronicle Volume 1]]'' Zandalar has accepted the tortollan as an exception to their troll-only policy due to the useful information they provide the trolls. The Zandalari did try to get rid of them once, but the tortollans managed to change the mind of then-[[Tezlekhan|King Tezlekhan]] using their political influence and information they had gathered on the royal family.[[Tortollan Seeker#Quotes]] ===Cataclysm=== {{cata-section}} The [[Cataclysm (event)|Cataclysm]] inflicted great damage on Zuldazar,{{mob|Prophet Khar'zul}}: {{text|say|We NEED dis land! Da cataclysm destroyed our home!}}[[The Dark Prophet Zul]][[Waterlogged Zandalari Journal]] causing the great palace of [[Rastakhan|King Rastakhan]] to list to one side, the forum to be flooded with sea water, jagged fissures tearing up the tiles, and high tides coming up to the market awnings. But while there was some damage, the city was rebuilt, after [[Zul]]'s departure.[[The Word of Zul (quest)]]: {{text|say|Dockmaster Cobo|He was wrong. Oh there was damage, but Zul fled, with our fleet, and started a few wars. Those of us who stayed, endured. We rebuilt. Because THAT is what it means to be a Zandalari.}} ===Battle for Azeroth=== {{bfa-section}} Years later, as conflict once again erupted between the [[Alliance]] and [[Horde]], the [[blood troll]]s made greater and greater incursions into Zuldazar from [[Nazmir]]. Princess Talanji, frustrated from her father's inadequate response to this threat, sought outside help from the Horde, but she was intercepted by the Alliance. After the Horde saved Zul and [[Talanji]] from the [[Stormwind Stockades]], Zandalar let the Horde establish an embassy within the pyramid of [[Dazar'alor]]. Some time later, [[Zul]] launched an insurrection against Rastakhan. With Zandalar opening its borders to non-trolls, other races such as [[tol'vir]] and [[tuskarr]] traveled to Zuldazar's port to do trade.[[Shakedown]] Zuldazar was raided by the [[Alliance]] during [[Battle of Dazar'alor]] which resulted in the death of King [[Rastakhan]] and the crippling of the [[Golden Fleet]]. ===The War Within=== {{tww-section}} With the Zandalari's permission, the Bilgewater goblins have expanded their kaja'mite mining operations in Zuldazar.[[Hexlord Raal]] dialogue at Kaja'Coast Across the mountains southwest of Gorilla Gorge, they have established the [[Kaja'Coast]]. However, [[Jastor Gallywix]] and the [[Venture Company]] took over the operation and began shipping it to [[Undermine]],[[Crashing the Market]] where it is used to make containers that can safely hold the [[Black Blood]] of the [[Old Gods]].[[B.I.R.D. Watching]] Against the Zandalari's wishes, Venture blew up a mountain sacred to the [[loa]] [[Pa'ku]] in order to mine more kaja'mite. Furious, [[Hexlord Raal]] declared that even though Bilgewater was not the group responsible it was still their leader [[Monte Gazlowe]]'s responsibility to fix it. ==Getting there== The main way to travel here is to use the portal in the Portal Room ([[Pathfinder's Den]]) in [[Orgrimmar]]. But there is also a boat that departs from the [[Echo Isles]] in [[Durotar]]. As the [[Alliance War Campaign]] progresses, [[Grand Admiral Jes-Tereth]] allows access to the area. ==Geography== The region consists of lush, tropical environments with ancient, mountainous terrain. Thousands of cannibalistic [[jungle troll]]s inhabit these ziggurats. Zuldazar is the seat of [[Rastakhan|King Rastakhan]] and hosts a gathering of all the troll tribes every six years; the [[troll]]s meet to share information and plot (most likely).''[[Lands of Mystery]]'', pg. 81 - 82 ==Notes and trivia== *The {{Ref WoWCV1}} art for Zuldazar draws inspiration from the {{wp|Inca Empire|Inca}} citadel {{wp|Machu Picchu}} and combines it with the architecture of the {{wp|Aztec Empire|Aztec}} and the {{wp|Maya civilization|Maya}}. *All the zones of [[Zandalar]] have been referred to as either being a jewel or the heart of the [[Zandalari Empire]]. **[[Vol'dun]] was once a lush jungle and the jewel of the troll empire.[[The Warguard's Trail]] **[[Nazmir]] was once a lush forest and is implied to have been the heart of the Zandalari civilization.[[Ancient Nazmani Tablet]] **Zuldazar in its prime was a massive, bustling [[temple city]] built across a mountain range, and is also considered the jewel of all troll civilizations.[[Welcome to Zuldazar]] *Although Dazar'alor is referred to as the city[[The Fall of Zuldazar]]: {{text|say|Master Mathias Shaw|An assault on the city of Dazar'alor will destabilize the Horde's relations with the Zandalari.}} (and is displayed as such on the map), Zuldazar as the city proper's name (as was the case before ''Battle for Azeroth'', when the island lacked distinct zones) is still occasionally implied. *The Visitor's Guide called Zandalar a "subcontinent". ==Speculation== {{speculation}} Taking all of the notes above into consideration and combining it with the fact that Zuldazar has always been the Zandalari capital, and every region has [[loa]] temples—required to form a temple city—and that all Zandalari ruins across Zandalar are connected to each other as well as the loa temples, it is possible that Zuldazar at its height covered all of modern Zandalar. In fact, Zuldazar most likely stretched far beyond the borders of modern Zandalar in the past, as most of what was once the Zandalar Mountains is today beneath the waves as a result of the [[Great Sundering]]. Notably, [[Nazwatha]] in Nazmir has a massive road enclosed by buildings extending far into the ocean from the pyramid, meanwhile the [[:File:Zuldazar.jpg|official art]] of Zuldazar from ''[[World of Warcraft: Chronicle Volume 1|Chronicle Volume 1]]'' shows a part of Zuldazar that did not make it into ''[[World of Warcraft: Battle for Azeroth|Battle for Azeroth]]'' (though inspiring [[Atal'Dazar]]), while also showing that the city had massive structures and plateaus built up against the sides of tall mountains, those parts of the mountain range now being lost beneath the sea. ==Gallery== File:Zandalar.PNG|Zandalar in the RPG with Zuldazar's location File:Blizzcon 2017 - Zuldazar 1.jpg|BlizzCon 2017 screenshot File:Blizzcon 2017 - Zuldazar 2.jpg|BlizzCon 2017 screenshot File:Blizzcon 2017 - Zuldazar 3.jpg|BlizzCon 2017 screenshot File:Nightborne Camp in Zuldazar.jpg|Nightborne Camp File:Dark Iron Camp in Zuldazar.jpg|Dark Iron Camp File:Zuldazar - Brutosaur.jpg File:Zuldazar - Devilsaur.jpg File:Zuldazar - Loa shrine.jpg File:Zuldazar - Riverbeasts.jpg File:Zuldazar - Stairs.jpg ;Concept art File:Zandalar jungle concept.jpg File:Zandalar jungle concept 2.jpg File:Zuldazar Wall concept.jpg File:Zuldazar concept art 1.jpg File:Zuldazar concept art 2.jpg File:Zuldazar concept art 3.jpg File:Zuldazar concept art 4.jpg File:Zuldazar concept by Chris Deboda.jpg File:Zuldazar concept by Chris Deboda 2.jpg File:Zuldazar plant paintover.jpg|Paintover exploring ideas for jungle plants File:Zuldazar logo.jpg|Zuldazar logo ==Patch changes== *{{Patch 11.1.0|note=[[Kaja'Coast]] subzone added.}} *{{Patch 8.0.1|note=Added.}} ==References== {{Reflist}} ==External links== {|class=darktable |{{Elinks-zone|8499}} |{{Elinks-zone|9570}} |} {{Zuldazar}} {{Zandalar}} [[Category:Zuldazar| ]] [[Category:Zandalar]] [[Category:Zandalari troll territories]] [[Category:Temple cities]] [[Category:Lands of Mystery]]
